questions.q: A 32-year-old farmer presents with multiple painless nodular lesions along the lymphatics of the forearm after a thorn prick. Skin biopsy shows asteroid bodies within giant cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Sporotrichosis (Sporothrix schenckii) classically presents with lymphocutaneous spread after traumatic inoculation. Asteroid bodies (Splendore-Hoeppli phenomenon) are characteristic. Treatment is itraconazole.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman with SLE develops a butterfly-shaped erythema across the nose and cheeks sparing the nasolabial folds. Which immunofluorescence finding at the dermoepidermal junction would confirm this diagnosis?
opts: IgA deposits in a granular pattern
IgG deposits in a linear pattern
IgG and C3 deposits in a granular pattern
IgA deposits in a linear pattern
questions.exp: In SLE, DIF shows granular deposits of IgG, IgM, IgA and C3 at the DEJ (lupus band test), positive in both lesional and non-lesional sun-exposed skin.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin with negative Nikolsky sign. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae, negative Nikolsky sign, and DIF showing linear IgG and C3 at BMZ. Target antigen is BP180 (collagen XVII) and BP230.

questions.q: A 28-year-old sexually active man presents with painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis with clean base and raised edges. Inguinal lymphadenopathy is firm, non-tender and rubbery. What is the drug of choice?
opts: Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days
Benzathine penicillin 2.4 MU single IM dose
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 3 days
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) is the diagnosis. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose is the drug of choice. Doxycycline is used in penicillin allergy.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden onset of tender erythematous nodules over the face and extremities with fever, and laboratory tests show neutrophilia with elevated CRP. What type of lepra reaction is this?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL/Type 2 reaction) occurs in BL/LL leprosy, characterized by tender erythematous nodules, fever, and systemic involvement. It is an immune complex-mediated (Type III) reaction. Treatment is thalidomide or prednisolone.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with progressive proximal muscle weakness, violaceous erythema of the eyelids (heliotrope rash), and Gottron papules over the MCPJs. Serum CK is markedly elevated. Which antibody is associated with highest risk of interstitial lung disease?
questions.exp: Anti-MDA5 antibody in dermatomyositis is strongly associated with clinically amyopathic dermatomyositis and rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease (RP-ILD), which carries a poor prognosis.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male presents with well-demarcated silvery scaly plaques over extensor surfaces of knees and elbows. On removing the scale, pinpoint bleeding is observed. What is the name for this clinical sign?
questions.exp: Auspitz sign (positive in psoriasis) is the appearance of pinpoint bleeding points when a psoriatic scale is removed, due to elongation of dermal papillae with thinning of the suprapapillary plate.

questions.q: A 20-year-old presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the genitalia with tingling and burning. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. The patient is immunocompetent. What is the first-line treatment?
opts: Acyclovir 200 mg five times daily for 5 days
Famciclovir 250 mg three times daily for 5 days
Acyclovir 400 mg three times daily for 7-10 days
questions.exp: For primary genital herpes in immunocompetent patients, Acyclovir 400 mg TID for 7-10 days (or 200 mg 5x/day) is standard. Valacyclovir 1g BD for 10 days is equally effective and preferred for convenience.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with depigmented patches on the dorsa of hands and around the mouth. Wood's lamp examination shows chalky-white fluorescence. A skin biopsy shows complete absence of melanocytes. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Vitiligo is characterized by complete loss of melanocytes on biopsy, chalky-white fluorescence on Wood's lamp, and depigmented macules/patches. The other options show reduced (not absent) melanocytes.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male with a long history of sun exposure presents with a pearly, telangiectatic, rolled-edge nodule on his nose that bleeds on minimal trauma. The most appropriate treatment for a 1 cm lesion on the nose is:
opts: Wide local excision with 2 cm margins
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma on the nose (H-zone face) requires tissue-sparing technique with complete margin control. Mohs micrographic surgery is the gold standard for high-risk BCC on the face.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the mouth and nose following an upper respiratory tract infection. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Impetigo contagiosa is predominantly caused by Staphylococcus aureus (gram-positive cocci in clusters), though Group A Streptococcus can also cause it. The honey-colored crust is characteristic.

questions.q: Which of the following drug combinations is used in paucibacillary (PB) leprosy according to WHO MDT regimen?
questions.exp: WHO MDT for PB leprosy: Rifampicin 600 mg monthly (supervised) + Dapsone 100 mg daily (unsupervised) for 6 months. MB leprosy uses a three-drug regimen including Clofazimine for 12 months.

questions.q: A 22-year-old sexually active woman presents with multiple soft, painless, flesh-colored papules on the vulva. HPV typing of the biopsy specimens shows HPV 6 and 11. What is the appropriate initial treatment?
questions.exp: Condylomata acuminata (genital warts) caused by HPV 6/11 can be treated with patient-applied topical imiquimod 5% cream (immunomodulator) 3 times/week for up to 16 weeks. Podophyllotoxin is also provider-applied option.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with recurrent oral erosions and flaccid bullae on the trunk. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposits ('fish-net' pattern) in the epidermis. The target antigen is on which protein?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris targets Desmoglein 3 (mucous membrane involvement predominant) and Desmoglein 1 (skin involvement). DIF shows intercellular IgG in a 'fish-net' or chicken-wire pattern.

questions.q: A patient with leprosy is classified as borderline tuberculoid (BT). Histopathology of skin biopsy shows epithelioid cell granulomas with giant cells along cutaneous nerves, sparse lymphocytic infiltrate, and no bacilli on Wade-Fite stain. What is the bacterial index?
questions.exp: In tuberculoid and BT leprosy, bacterial index (BI) is 0 (paucibacillary), as few or no bacilli are detectable on Ziehl-Neelsen or Wade-Fite staining. BI is used to classify leprosy into PB vs MB.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with pruritic, symmetrically distributed erythematous papulovesicles on the extensor surfaces and buttocks. DIF shows granular IgA deposits at the dermal papillae tips. What is the associated systemic condition?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is associated with celiac disease/gluten-sensitive enteropathy in nearly all cases. DIF shows granular IgA at dermal papillae tips. Treatment is dapsone + gluten-free diet.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a verrucous plaque on the lower leg developing over 5 years. Biopsy shows 'copper penny' or 'medlar bodies' (muriform cells). What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is caused by dematiaceous fungi (most commonly Fonsecaea pedrosoi). Characteristic finding is muriform cells (sclerotic bodies/copper pennies) in tissue. Lesions are verrucous plaques, usually on feet/legs.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman on oral contraceptives develops bilateral symmetrical hyperpigmented patches over the cheeks, nose and forehead. Wood's lamp enhances the pigmentation. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Melasma treatment: Kligman's triple combination formula (hydroquinone 5% + tretinoin 0.1% + hydrocortisone 1%) is the gold standard. Sun protection is mandatory. OCP should be discontinued if possible.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male patient receiving long-term clofazimine for leprosy develops brownish-black skin pigmentation. Clofazimine acts primarily by:
opts: Interfering with mycobacterial DNA by binding to guanine bases
questions.exp: Clofazimine is a phenazine dye that binds preferentially to mycobacterial DNA (guanine residues), inhibiting template function. It also has anti-inflammatory properties via inhibition of TNF-alpha and lymphocyte proliferation.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with a rapidly growing nodule on the lower leg over 3 months. Histology shows pleomorphic spindle cells with atypical mitoses, high Ki-67 index, arranged in herringbone pattern. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma (formerly MFH) is the most common soft tissue sarcoma in older adults, presenting as rapidly growing pleomorphic spindle cell tumor with herringbone/storiform pattern and atypical mitoses.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most common type of skin cancer worldwide and is characterised by palisading basal cells at the periphery of tumor nests on histology?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer worldwide. Histology shows nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artifact. It has very low metastatic potential.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman presents with thickened, tender skin over the fingertips with pitting scars, Raynaud's phenomenon, and difficulty swallowing. ANA is positive with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase-I). What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase-I) antibody is associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc), which has a higher risk of pulmonary fibrosis and renal crisis. Anti-centromere antibodies are associated with lcSSc (CREST).

questions.q: A 25-year-old atopic patient presents with chronic pruritic, lichenified plaques in the antecubital and popliteal fossae. Serum IgE levels are markedly elevated. Which cytokines are primarily responsible for IgE class switching in this condition?
questions.exp: In atopic dermatitis, Th2 cytokines IL-4 and IL-13 drive IgE class switching by inducing isotype switching in B cells. IL-4 also upregulates FcεRI and promotes mast cell activity. Dupilumab (anti-IL-4Rα) targets this pathway.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with multiple small perifollicular papules and pustules on the upper trunk, worsened by sweating and scratching. KOH preparation of skin scrapings shows short curved hyphae and clusters of round yeast cells ('spaghetti and meatballs'). What is the appropriate treatment?
opts: Oral terbinafine 250 mg daily for 4 weeks
Oral itraconazole 200 mg daily for 7 days
questions.exp: Malassezia folliculitis (Pityrosporum folliculitis) is caused by Malassezia furfur, showing 'spaghetti and meatballs' on KOH. Oral itraconazole is effective for widespread/recalcitrant cases. Topical antifungals are first-line for mild cases.

questions.q: A 22-year-old man presents with a painless groin ulcer followed by massive inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo). Frei's test (Lygranum test) is positive. What is the etiologic agent?
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3. It is characterised by a transient painless papule/ulcer followed by bubo formation. Frei's skin test (now obsolete) was previously diagnostic.

questions.q: A 44-year-old man presents with a non-healing painful ulcer with beefy-red granulation tissue and rolled edges on the penis. Giemsa staining of tissue smear reveals intracytoplasmic encapsulated organisms within macrophages. What are these called?
questions.exp: Donovanosis (granuloma inguinale) is caused by Klebsiella granulomatis. Donovan bodies are intracytoplasmic encapsulated organisms within mononuclear cells, best seen on Giemsa or Warthin-Starry stain.

questions.q: A 32-year-old man presents with a painless chance-like lesion on the finger. He works as a butcher. Gram stain shows filamentous gram-positive organisms. Culture on blood agar shows characteristic 'bottle brush' colonies. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Erysipeloid is caused by Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, a gram-positive filamentous bacillus affecting butchers, fishermen, and veterinarians. Presents as violaceous, painful spreading lesion (not a true chancre) on finger/hand.

questions.q: A patient receiving isotretinoin for nodulocystic acne asks about monitoring. Which of the following laboratory parameters is most critical to monitor monthly?
opts: Serum triglycerides and liver function tests
questions.exp: Isotretinoin can cause hypertriglyceridemia (risk of pancreatitis) and hepatotoxicity. Monthly monitoring of fasting lipid profile and LFTs is mandatory. Pregnancy test (beta-hCG) is also mandatory in females.

questions.q: Which layer of the epidermis contains the enzyme transglutaminase-1 responsible for the formation of cornified cell envelope?
questions.exp: Transglutaminase-1 (keratinocyte TGase) is expressed in the stratum granulosum and is responsible for cross-linking structural proteins (loricrin, involucrin) to form the cornified cell envelope. Mutations cause lamellar ichthyosis.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man with HIV (CD4 = 80 cells/µL) presents with multiple violaceous nodules on the lower extremities, oral palate, and cutaneous lymphedema. Biopsy shows spindle cells, slit-like vascular spaces, and extravasated red blood cells. What is the causative herpesvirus?
questions.exp: AIDS-associated Kaposi sarcoma is caused by HHV-8 (Kaposi Sarcoma-associated Herpesvirus/KSHV). Histology shows spindle cells, irregular vascular channels, and extravasated erythrocytes. Treatment includes HAART and liposomal doxorubicin.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with recurrent 'sausage digit' dactylitis of the right index finger, nail pitting (>20 pits), onycholysis, and scaly plaques on the scalp and elbows. Joint X-ray shows 'pencil-in-cup' deformity. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Psoriatic arthritis presents with psoriatic skin/nail changes plus inflammatory arthritis. Dactylitis ('sausage digit') and 'pencil-in-cup' deformity on X-ray are characteristic. RF is negative (seronegative spondyloarthropathy).
